description: Answer multiple-choice questions spanning 57 academic and professional subjects.
input: Subject question with four answer choices
output: One selected answer
assessment: Accuracy against the answer key

description: Solve contest math problems with exact final answers; the dataset also provides worked solutions.
input: Competition math problem
output: Final mathematical answer, optionally with working
assessment: Normalized final answer compared with the reference

description: Compare language models across diverse contributed tasks rather than one fixed exam format.
input: Task-specific prompt, sometimes with answer choices
output: Generated text or scores for candidate answers
assessment: Task-defined metric; no single universal grader

description: Complete a Python function from its signature and docstring, then run unit tests.
input: Python function signature, docstring and examples
output: Function implementation
assessment: Unit-test success, summarized as pass@k

description: Answer questions designed to elicit common human misconceptions rather than repeat them.
input: Question targeting a common misconception
output: Free answer, selected option or candidate answer likelihoods
assessment: Truthfulness and informativeness judgments; separate multiple-choice metrics

description: Compare answers to ambiguous and disambiguated questions to see when a model relies on stereotypes.
input: Ambiguous or disambiguated vignette, question and choices
output: One choice, including “unknown”
assessment: Answer accuracy and stereotype bias by context type

description: Translate a word problem into several arithmetic steps and return a numerical answer.
input: Grade-school math word problem
output: Numerical final answer, optionally with working
assessment: Final number matched against the reference answer

description: Write complete programs for competition problems and check them against input/output test cases.
input: Programming problem with input/output specification
output: Complete runnable program
assessment: Program output checked on test cases

description: Compare models on the same scenarios across metrics such as accuracy, calibration and efficiency.
input: Scenario-specific text prompts or answer choices
output: Generations or likelihoods, depending on scenario
assessment: Scenario-specific metrics including accuracy, robustness and calibration

description: Collect blind head-to-head votes on two model responses to a user’s own prompt.
input: User prompt shared with two anonymous models
output: Two competing conversational responses
assessment: Users vote head-to-head; votes determine relative ratings

description: Learn successive language-conditioned manipulation tasks and test how earlier skills transfer.
input: Language instruction and robot observations across tasks
output: Robot actions in a manipulation episode
assessment: Simulated task success across the learning sequence

description: Answer image-based multiple-choice questions; rotating answer choices tests consistency.
input: Image, question and rotating multiple-choice options
output: One answer per rotation
assessment: Correct across every rotation in CircularEval

description: Complete instructions on working replicas of websites; check what actually changed on the site.
input: User goal and an interactive replica website
output: Browser actions and, when requested, a written answer
assessment: Task-specific checks on page state, URL or answer

description: Read long English and Chinese inputs for tasks such as question answering, summarization and code completion.
input: Long English or Chinese context and task prompt
output: Answer, summary, label or code completion
assessment: Task-specific scores such as F1, ROUGE or code similarity

description: Modify a real Python repository to resolve a GitHub issue; regression tests judge the patch.
input: Repository snapshot and corresponding GitHub issue
output: Patch to the repository
assessment: Required issue-fixing and regression tests must pass

description: Recover an inserted fact as the length of the surrounding text and the fact’s position change.
input: Long passage with a planted fact and question
output: Answer recalling the planted information
assessment: Original harness: model-graded recall by length and depth

description: Answer expert-written multiple-choice science questions designed to challenge knowledgeable nonexperts.
input: Expert-written science question and four options
output: One selected answer
assessment: Accuracy against expert-provided answer keys

description: Answer practical questions that require combinations of browsing, file handling, tools and reasoning.
input: Real-world question, sometimes with an attached file
output: Short text, number or list
assessment: Normalized final answer matched against the reference

description: Interpret discipline-specific visuals such as diagrams and charts to solve college-level problems.
input: College-level subject question and associated visuals
output: Selected option or open-ended answer
assessment: Choice accuracy or rule-based open-answer matching

description: Evaluate whether systems resist requests for harmful behavior under a common evaluation protocol.
input: Test prompt targeting a specified harmful behavior
output: Model response to the test prompt
assessment: Behavior classifier labels responses; report attack success rate

description: Select a function and its arguments, handle parallel calls, or withhold a call when none fits.
input: User request and available function signatures
output: Function calls with arguments, or no call
assessment: Syntax-tree matching or execution checks by category

description: Use time-stamped contest problems to test code generation, repair, execution and output prediction.
input: Dated contest problem, code or execution example
output: Program, repair, execution result or predicted output
assessment: Test-case success or answer matching, by subtask

description: Increase input length while varying retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation and question answering.
input: Synthetic long context and a task-specific query
output: Retrieved values, aggregates or short answers
assessment: Reference-string coverage or any-match, depending on task

description: Operate real desktop applications and verify the resulting operating-system or application state.
input: Natural-language instruction and initialized desktop environment
output: Desktop actions that change applications or files
assessment: Task-specific execution checks on the resulting state

description: Answer questions about short through hour-long videos, with or without subtitles and audio.
input: Video and multiple-choice question; optional audio or subtitles
output: One selected answer
assessment: Answer accuracy, broken down by video duration

description: Converse with a simulated customer and call tools; check the final database state against the goal.
input: Simulated customer, domain policy, tools and database
output: Tool actions and messages to the customer
assessment: Final database state and required reply contents checked

description: Run the SWE-bench repair task on a human-validated subset of 500 issues.
input: Human-validated issue and matching repository snapshot
output: Patch to the repository
assessment: Same test-based resolution criterion, on 500 validated issues

description: Train and submit models for Kaggle competitions, then compare their scores with human submissions.
input: Competition brief, dataset and submission specification
output: Submission file with test-set predictions
assessment: Competition metric and medal thresholds from human standings

description: Recall, update and connect facts from earlier conversations, and abstain when the answer is absent.
input: Timestamped chat sessions and a later question
output: Answer from memory, or an explicit abstention
assessment: Model judge checks correctness against a reference

description: Solve original expert-written math problems with answers that can be verified automatically.
input: Original advanced mathematics problem
output: Numerical answer or specified mathematical object
assessment: Verification script checks the answer or its properties

description: Compare agents with human specialists on seven open-ended research engineering tasks under time budgets.
input: Open-ended ML engineering goal and timed environment
output: Working solution in the task environment
assessment: Normalized task-specific scores compared with time-budgeted human attempts

description: Answer closed-ended expert questions across disciplines, including questions that require images.
input: Expert question, sometimes with an image
output: Selected or short answer with stated confidence
assessment: Paper reports model-judged accuracy and RMS calibration error

description: Turn visual observations into actions for navigation, manipulation and other simulated tasks.
input: Embodied instruction and visual observations in a simulator
output: High-level plans or lower-level actions, by environment
assessment: Task success rate in the simulator

description: Infer a transformation rule from example grid pairs and apply it to a new grid.
input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test input
output: Predicted output grid
assessment: Dimensions and every cell must match the target

description: Reproduce ML papers from scratch; graders inspect code, execution and experimental results against a rubric.
input: ML paper, clarifications and a replication environment
output: Code, execution instructions and resulting research artifacts
assessment: Model grader scores weighted, author-developed rubric items

description: Complete multi-step tasks in a terminal; task-specific tests inspect the final environment.
input: Terminal task instruction and a prepared container
output: Shell actions and resulting files or system state
assessment: Task-specific tests determine completion

description: Improve a model or its training and inference pipeline against a held-out objective under a fixed budget.
input: Open-ended AI engineering objective and fixed compute budget
output: Training, inference or agent-harness changes
assessment: Task metric normalized to best valid trial; two-trial average

description: Infer a new transformation rule from example grids; reproduce the target grid without a written instruction.
input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test grid
output: Predicted output grid
assessment: Grid dimensions and all cell values must match

description: Read a document page to answer a question grounded in its text and layout.
input: Document page image and natural-language question
output: Short answer extracted from the document
assessment: Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity against reference answers

description: Compare models across code search, translation, completion and other programming-language tasks.
input: Code, text queries or paired snippets, by subtask
output: Labels, rankings, code or documentation
assessment: Task-specific metrics including accuracy, F1 and BLEU

description: Write Python programs that meet a problem specification; passing some tests differs from solving the problem.
input: Programming problem and required input/output behavior
output: Python solution program
assessment: Fraction of tests passed and all-tests accuracy

description: Translate a short English programming task into a Python function that satisfies its tests.
input: Short Python task description and test assertions
output: Python program implementing the requested behavior
assessment: Generated code run against unit tests

description: Read plotted values and reason across them to answer questions about a chart.
input: Chart and natural-language question
output: Short textual or numerical answer
assessment: Answer accuracy with tolerance for numerical responses

description: Search a simulated online shop and buy a product that meets a shopper’s requirements.
input: Shopping request and simulated online store
output: Searches, page actions and final product selection
assessment: Reward for matching requested attributes, options and price

description: Solve school-level science questions; the dataset includes explanations as well as answer choices.
input: Science question, choices and optional image or context
output: Selected answer; explanations can also be generated
assessment: Choice accuracy; explanation quality evaluated separately

description: Test reasoning on a deliberately difficult subset of 23 existing BIG-bench tasks.
input: Task prompt with choices or short-answer format
output: Final choice or task-specific answer
assessment: Accuracy against reference answers across 23 tasks

description: Solve objective questions from academic and professional exams, including free-response and multiple-choice items.
input: Exam question, sometimes with supplied answer choices
output: Selected choice or filled-in answer
assessment: Choice accuracy; exact match or F1 for blanks

description: Determine when to find and call an API, execute it and respond in the ongoing dialogue.
input: User dialogue, API descriptions and execution environment
output: API calls and follow-up dialogue responses
assessment: API-call correctness; ROUGE-L for follow-up responses

description: Evaluate generated programs more rigorously by extending the tests for an existing synthesis benchmark.
input: Python synthesis prompts from the underlying benchmark
output: Python function implementations
assessment: Pass@k under expanded functional test suites

description: Translate a question into SQL over large, real databases where correctness and query efficiency both matter.
input: Database, schema, question and external knowledge
output: Executable SQL query
assessment: Execution accuracy and efficiency of correct queries

description: Probe whether a vision-language model claims an object is present when it is absent from the image.
input: Image and yes/no object-presence question
output: Yes or no
assessment: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and yes-answer rate

description: Predict each next action from demonstrations of real websites, rather than driving a live browser.
input: Task, webpage snapshot and action history
output: Target element, operation and optional value
assessment: Element accuracy, operation F1 and step/task success

description: Ask paired yes/no questions about each image to test visual recognition and reasoning.
input: Image and paired yes/no questions
output: Yes or no for each question
assessment: Per-question accuracy plus accuracy requiring both answers correct

description: Resolve user requests by planning and executing API calls; compare the resulting solution paths.
input: User instruction and available API documentation
output: Tool-call trajectory and final answer
assessment: ToolEval model judges task pass rate and pairwise wins

description: Operate in multiple environments, from databases to games; each environment defines its own objective.
input: Task, environment state and available actions
output: Sequence of environment-specific actions or responses
assessment: Environment-specific success or reward, then aggregate scoring

description: Combine a diagram, chart or other visual with mathematical reasoning to solve a question.
input: Visual math problem and optional answer choices
output: Choice or free-form mathematical answer
assessment: Extracted answer normalized and matched to reference

description: Run and modify ML experiments under constraints to meet a specified research or engineering goal.
input: Research brief, files, tools and evaluation metric
output: Task-specified artifact such as test predictions
assessment: Task-specific objectives scored against benchmark success criteria

description: Follow natural-language constraints whose satisfaction can be checked without a human or model judge.
input: Prompt with one or more verifiable constraints
output: One generated text response
assessment: Rule checks; strict/loose prompt- and instruction-level accuracy

description: Choose the answer to questions designed to require interpretation of events over time, not just a single frame.
input: Video clip and multiple-choice temporal question
output: Selected answer choice
assessment: Answer accuracy across temporal tasks

description: Solve bilingual competition problems, distinguishing automatically scored final answers from proof problems.
input: Olympiad problem, sometimes with a diagram
output: Mathematical or physical answer; some problems request proof
assessment: Reported automatic accuracy covers non-proof final answers

description: Answer harder, reasoning-oriented academic questions with more distractors than the original MMLU.
input: Multisubject question with up to ten options
output: Selected answer choice
assessment: Accuracy against answer keys across subjects

description: Investigate a simulated world by conducting experiments, then explain the mechanisms discovered.
input: Scientific scenario in an interactive simulated world
output: Experimental actions and discovered explanatory knowledge
assessment: Task completion, procedural progress and explanatory knowledge accuracy

description: Analyze supplied datasets and propose a hypothesis that specifies the context, variables and their relationship.
input: Dataset, metadata and discovery question
output: Natural-language hypothesis supported by the analysis
assessment: Model-assisted hypothesis match on context, variables and relation

description: Answer multiple-choice questions about the interpretation of scientific literature, figures and research data.
input: Biology research question with answer options
output: Selected answer or abstention
assessment: Accuracy, precision on attempted questions and coverage

description: Answer questions over realistic spreadsheets or build predictions for modeling competitions.
input: Business-analysis spreadsheets or competition modeling datasets
output: Analysis answers or test-set predictions
assessment: Answer correctness or competition-specific predictive performance

description: Use a paper’s code repository to reproduce outputs and answer questions about the resulting artifacts.
input: Reproducibility questions and a computational research repository
output: Answers derived from reproduced outputs
assessment: Answers checked against reference results for each task

description: Generate a runnable analysis program that produces the requested scientific result from supplied data.
input: Scientific task, dataset and optional expert guidance
output: Python program and its executed results
assessment: Task-specific success; code similarity and cost also reported

description: Carry out a sequence of household chores from a high-level goal and step-by-step instructions in AI2-THOR.
input: Household instructions and an egocentric view
output: Navigation and object-interaction actions
assessment: Full task success and fraction of goal conditions met; path-weighted variants are also reported

description: Measure how often continuing ordinary web text produces toxic language, including after non-toxic prompts.
input: A sentence fragment from the web
output: Multiple sampled text continuations
assessment: Perspective toxicity scores; expected maximum toxicity and probability of at least one toxic continuation

description: Test whether a robot can execute consecutive language instructions without resetting between subtasks.
input: A sequence of language commands and robot observations
output: Arm and gripper controls for each step
assessment: Environment checks each subtask; report success by chain length and mean completed length

description: Distinguish implicit hate speech from benign statements mentioning the same minority groups.
input: One statement about a group
output: Toxicity label or classifier score
assessment: Compare against labeled examples; the paper reports ROC AUC for detection experiments

description: In VIMA-Bench, infer an object-manipulation task from interleaved text and images and carry it out in simulation.
input: Multimodal prompt and current scene views
output: A sequence of pose-parameterized manipulation actions
assessment: Episode success averaged over tasks within each of four generalization levels

description: Evaluate rigid- and soft-body manipulation policies on object variations in the SAPIEN simulator.
input: Simulated robot and object observations; task-specific goal
output: Continuous robot controls under the chosen controller
assessment: Task-specific simulator success conditions; aggregate success over evaluation episodes

description: Compare achievement rewards with the ethical consequences of an agent’s choices in branching text adventures.
input: A game scene and its available choices
output: One action choice at each decision point
assessment: Game rewards and annotated trajectory measures for ethical violations, disutility and power

description: Benchmark a robot on multi-stage furniture assembly from different initial part configurations.
input: Camera views and robot state for an assembly task
output: Arm motion and gripper actions
assessment: Assembly success across trials and number of completed phases for partial progress

description: Compare model behavior across eight trust dimensions, including stereotypes, privacy, robustness and fairness.
input: A scenario-specific prompt, examples or classification input
output: A generated response or predicted label
assessment: Scenario-specific measures such as accuracy, toxicity scores and group fairness gaps

description: Compare exact-answer tasks and open-ended requests grounded in long documents.
input: Long input document and an instruction
output: Short answer, selected option or extended response
assessment: Exact-match-style scores for closed tasks; overlap metrics, model judging or human review for open tasks

description: Identify safe requests that a model wrongly refuses because their wording resembles an unsafe request.
input: A benign prompt with potentially sensitive wording
output: A free-text reply
assessment: In the original protocol, label compliance, partial refusal or full refusal and report refusal rates

description: Test recognition of appropriate decisions across safety categories using Chinese and English questions.
input: A safety question and multiple answer choices
output: One selected answer
assessment: Accuracy against the answer key, reported by language and safety category

description: The original suite measures insecure code suggestions and whether assistants comply with unsafe requests.
input: A coding task or a safety-test request
output: A code suggestion or short response
assessment: Separate rates of flagged insecure code and of responses judged compliant; not a system penetration test

description: Compare model responses across a hierarchy of safety topics using open-response and multiple-choice tests.
input: A safety question or a multiple-choice variant
output: Free-text response or selected options
assessment: MD-Judge labels open responses for safety; the multiple-choice subset uses its answer keys

description: Distinguish answers that merely avoid refusing from answers that meaningfully satisfy a prohibited request.
input: A benchmark request and the assistant’s response
output: A graded judgment of the response
assessment: Original rubric combines refusal, specificity and convincingness into a graded score

description: Evaluate retrieval, reading and code reasoning on real and synthetic inputs exceeding 100K tokens on average.
input: A long context and task-specific question or instruction
output: A retrieved value, answer, choice or summary
assessment: Task-specific scoring, including answer matching, QA F1 and ROUGE for summarization

description: Retrieve facts from months of dialogue and reconstruct the speakers’ past events; the suite also tests dialogue generation.
input: Multi-session dialogue plus a question or event-summary request
output: A short answer or an account of relevant events
assessment: QA uses normalized answer F1; event summaries use ROUGE and factual precision/recall measures

description: Measure recall of domain knowledge used as a proxy for risk; the exam does not demonstrate practical capability.
input: A multiple-choice question in one of three domains
output: One selected answer
assessment: Multiple-choice accuracy per domain; compare utility separately when evaluating unlearning

description: Specify everyday activities as initial and goal conditions for agents in simulated household scenes.
input: An activity specification and simulated observations
output: Navigation and manipulation actions
assessment: Check final goal conditions for task success; the paper also reports efficiency measures

description: Compare the robustness of assistant responses under a standardized evaluation protocol.
input: A benchmark request describing a disallowed behavior
output: An assistant response
assessment: Judge whether the response fulfills the disallowed behavior; report the fraction of successful cases

description: Evaluate a robot on language-specified kitchen activities across layouts, objects and scene styles.
input: A kitchen task instruction and robot camera observations
output: Arm, gripper and optional mobile-base actions
assessment: Task-specific environment checks; report the success rate over trials

description: Answer bAbI questions whose supporting facts are separated by unrelated natural text.
input: A long passage containing task facts, followed by a question
output: A short answer inferred from those facts
assessment: Compare with the reference answer; report accuracy by reasoning task and context length

description: Compare recall with downstream tasks such as passage ranking, citation-grounded answers and summarization.
input: Long context and a task-specific query
output: An answer, ranked passage IDs, summary or task label
assessment: Task-specific metrics by context length; e.g., nDCG@10 for passage ranking and model-based summary grading

description: Answer questions requiring reasoning over long documents, code repositories, dialogue or structured data.
input: Long context, a question and four options
output: One selected option
assessment: Answer-key accuracy, with results broken down by difficulty and context length

description: Follow natural-language manipulation requests and test whether a policy can complete long-horizon goals.
input: An instruction and visual observations from the simulated scene
output: Robot actions or an executable skill sequence
assessment: Interactive evaluation reports success and a progress score that gives credit for completed stages

description: Complete a business workflow across simulated SaaS systems and respect its policies.
input: Business request and starting application state
output: Tool actions and final state across apps
assessment: Assertions check outcomes and policy compliance

description: Traverse a directed graph represented in a long input instead of locating a single inserted fact.
input: Directed graph plus a node and query
output: Set of nodes at the requested depth or parents
assessment: Predicted node set scored against the reference; report split and length

description: A CLI agent post-trains a supplied base model for a target benchmark within a fixed compute budget.
input: Small base model, target task and fixed compute
output: Post-trained model
assessment: Held-out target performance aggregated across model–task pairs

description: Produce deliverables for professional tasks across 44 occupations.
input: Work brief and reference materials
output: A professional work product
assessment: Expert blind comparisons of model and human deliverables

description: Use personal context and files to complete a practical everyday task.
input: Personal task, context, reference files and tools
output: Personalized outcome or artifact
assessment: Rubric-based grading against the task and starting state

description: Answer time-aligned questions about a person’s ongoing activities in first-person video.
input: First-person video segment and question
output: Answer to the video question
assessment: Answers scored against annotated choices, by capability

description: Assess security fixes to real repositories while checking that previously working behavior still holds.
input: Repository and defensive audit task
output: Code changes resolving the identified weakness
assessment: Programmatic security and regression checks

description: Measure agents on controlled security tasks drawn from complex software projects.
input: A controlled software-security task
output: An independently verifiable task result
assessment: Task success rate on the specified version and project split

description: Compare agents on a controlled web-application security assessment with independent verification.
input: Controlled web application assessment
output: Verified assessment outcome
assessment: Success on the named test version

description: Carry out a request by coordinating tools across applications. The final Verified release revised prompts, checks and reference outcomes.
input: A task and an initialized software workspace
output: Tool actions and a completed workspace task
assessment: Task-specific scripts verify the outcome

description: Produce a professional deliverable in a shared workspace for a banking, consulting or legal assignment. This is the agent benchmark, not the tool-free APEX suite.
input: A professional brief, files and workplace applications
output: A client-ready answer or work product
assessment: Expert rubrics: full-task pass rate and mean criterion score

description: Explore an unfamiliar game, infer its goals and advance through levels. A solver can write code, but the benchmark grades its actions, not its source code.
input: Observations from an unfamiliar interactive environment
output: Actions that reach the level goals
assessment: Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), using human action baselines

description: Search the web for a hard-to-locate fact and return a short, verifiable answer.
input: A question and access to the web
output: A concise factual answer
assessment: Answer correctness against a reference, using the documented grader

description: Complete a task in Android apps. The environment checks the device state, not whether an action sequence matches a demonstration.
input: A user instruction and a configured Android device
output: UI actions that complete the requested task
assessment: Task-specific checks of the resulting device state

description: Implement a scientific computation from a problem description, often by composing smaller scientific subproblems.
input: A scientific problem and its component specifications
output: Executable Python code
assessment: Scientist-authored test cases assess subproblems and full solutions

description: Complete a researcher-defined workflow in a terminal. The deliverable is a scientific result, not just code: tasks include image reconstruction, sensor calibration and model fitting.
input: A research task, its input files and a configured terminal
output: A task-specific artifact such as a reconstructed image or a fitted model
assessment: Resolution rate: share of tasks whose required checks all pass

description: Write the next response to a patient or clinician. Each of 5,000 conversations has its own physician-written criteria for what a good answer should include or avoid.
input: A health conversation ending in a user or clinician message
output: One free-text response
assessment: A model grader checks weighted physician-written criteria; scores are averaged across conversations.

description: Implement an original engineering task in an existing repository. The tests check the requested behavior rather than matching a reference patch.
input: A repository at a fixed revision and an engineering brief
output: A committed code change
assessment: Pass rate under task-specific behavioral tests; v1.1 grades the submitted patch in a clean environment.

description: Artificial Analysis combines results from several evaluations into one model-level score. There is no single “Intelligence Index” question to solve.
input: A model’s results on the component evaluations for one index version
output: One composite index score
assessment: In v5.0.1, nine evaluations feed four categories weighted 25% each; normalization and within-category weights are version-specific.

description: Two models build web apps from the same request. A voter tries both apps before picking a favorite or declaring a tie.
input: The same user-supplied web development brief for two models
output: Two runnable web apps for side-by-side comparison
assessment: Pairwise user votes are aggregated into Bradley–Terry ratings; there is no fixed pass mark.

description: Build a playable Godot game from a design brief. The agent submits the project and demonstrates its behavior with replayable inputs.
input: A game specification, Godot workspace and shared assets
output: A complete game project and replayable input traces
assessment: A judge scores the replay for game mechanics, content depth, visual feedback and presentation.

description: Write a query for a database not seen in training, given a question and its schema.
input: A question and a relational schema
output: One SQL query
assessment: Report the evaluator: original exact-set match or later test-suite execution accuracy.

description: Write SQL from supplied database metadata and documentation. Lite is the text-to-SQL track, not the full Spider 2.0 agent workflow.
input: A question, database metadata and reference documentation
output: SQL for the target database dialect
assessment: Compare query results with the reference under the Lite execution evaluator.

description: Complete user requests across live websites. WebVoyager names both the original agent and the evaluation; this entry is the evaluation.
input: A user request and annotated browser screenshots in the visual setting
output: Browser actions and a final answer
assessment: Task success rate; distinguish human judgments from the automated visual judge.

description: Compare sentence and document embeddings across tasks such as retrieval, clustering and semantic similarity. This is the original text suite.
input: Text queries, passages or sentence pairs, depending on the task
output: Embedding vectors
assessment: Use each task’s metric and identify the suite or subset behind any reported average.

description: Transcribe read English audiobooks. The clean and other test splits are reported separately.
input: Spoken English audio
output: A text transcript
assessment: Word error rate on the specified split; lower is better.

description: Read text in images, answer text-dependent questions and extract document information. This is OCRBench, not OCRBench v2.
input: An image and a question or recognition instruction
output: A text answer or transcription
assessment: Count answers accepted by the official evaluator across its task categories.

description: Control a simulated robot to complete manipulation tasks with multiple variations. State precisely which tasks and observations are used.
input: A task instruction, camera observations and robot state in a common observation setting
output: Robot actions
assessment: Fraction of trials that satisfy each task’s success conditions.

description: Answer Chinese multiple-choice questions across 52 subjects spanning several levels of difficulty.
input: A Chinese question and four answer options
output: The selected option
assessment: Multiple-choice accuracy; specify the subject aggregation and prompting setup.

description: Play board games, card games and social-deduction games against other agents. GameBench scores strategic play; it does not ask the model to build a game.
input: Game rules and the current state; most are text, Hive can use an image
output: A move or action for the current turn
assessment: Aggregate pairwise game outcomes with a Bradley–Terry rating model.
